title: Why Is My Compressed Video Larger Than the Original?
description: A compressed video can be larger than its original when the new export uses more data per second or a less efficient codec.
direct: A compressed video can be larger than its original when the new export uses more data per second or a less efficient codec. Compare the actual files rather than assuming that a button labeled compress guarantees a smaller result.

cards.choice.heading: Start with the source
cards.choice.body: Many camera and downloaded videos are already compressed. Re-encoding creates a new set of choices about codec, dimensions and quality. Exporting a small source at a higher-quality setting cannot restore lost detail and may simply add bytes.
sections.explain.heading: Resolution alone does not decide bytes
sections.explain.body: A smaller frame can still be encoded at a higher bitrate. For the same duration, overall data rate largely controls file size, with container overhead also contributing. Repeating lossy compression on successive exports can accumulate artifacts, so make each trial from the best source.
sections.practice.heading: Keep the useful copy
sections.practice.body: Space Sheep Studio develops Phone Cleaner for iPhone. Its current listing supports quality presets, local HD and 4K compression, H.264 and HEVC exports and original/output size comparison. No fixed reduction or lossless re-encoding is promised. If the source already meets your sharing requirement, another conversion may be unnecessary. Deleting media is a separate decision that should wait until you have verified useful copies and any needed backup.

related.related.label: Related practical guide
steps.step-1.text: Select the original in Phone Cleaner: Photo & Video and choose a suitable compression preset. Export tools require Pro.
steps.step-2.text: Export a separate copy and compare the original and output file sizes in the app. Retain the source while you judge playback.
steps.step-3.text: If the output is larger, return to the original and choose a smaller suitable setting. Test the receiver’s playback compatibility before choosing HEVC solely for efficiency.
